title: CSRs and a private CA with openssl
summary: Make a CSR, inspect it, sign it with your own CA using an extfile, build fullchain.pem and verify it.

steps.title: From CSR to signed certificate
body: A **CSR** (certificate signing request) carries a public key and the names you want, signed with the matching private key. You send it to a CA; the private key never leaves your server.
openssl req -in leaf.csr -noout -text -verify     # read it; "verify OK" = self-signature fine
The CA signs it with an **extfile** that says exactly what the certificate may do:

`-CAcreateserial` makes `int.srl` to hand out serial numbers. **`x509 -req` ignores the CSR's extensions** unless you add `-copy_extensions copy` (OpenSSL 3), which is why the SAN is repeated in the extfile.

`-days 200` matches the public rule: since March 2026 a publicly trusted TLS certificate may last at most 200 days (100 from March 2027, 47 from March 2029). A private CA is not bound by it, but short lifetimes plus automated renewal are the habit to build.

steps.prompt: Put the steps that build a private CA chain in order.
lines: `openssl x509 -req -in int.csr -CA root.pem -CAkey root.key -CAcreateserial -extfile int.ext -out int.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in leaf.csr -CA int.pem -CAkey int.key -CAcreateserial -extfile leaf.ext -out leaf.pem`
also: `openssl x509 -req -in int.csr -CA root.pem -CAkey root.key -CAcreateserial -extfile int.ext -out int.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in leaf.csr -CA int.pem -CAkey int.key -CAcreateserial -extfile leaf.ext -out leaf.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in int.csr -CA root.pem -CAkey root.key -CAcreateserial -extfile int.ext -out int.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in leaf.csr -CA int.pem -CAkey int.key -CAcreateserial -extfile leaf.ext -out leaf.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in int.csr -CA root.pem -CAkey root.key -CAcreateserial -extfile int.ext -out int.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in leaf.csr -CA int.pem -CAkey int.key -CAcreateserial -extfile leaf.ext -out leaf.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in int.csr -CA root.pem -CAkey root.key -CAcreateserial -extfile int.ext -out int.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in leaf.csr -CA int.pem -CAkey int.key -CAcreateserial -extfile leaf.ext -out leaf.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in int.csr -CA root.pem -CAkey root.key -CAcreateserial -extfile int.ext -out int.pem`
`openssl x509 -req -in leaf.csr -CA int.pem -CAkey int.key -CAcreateserial -extfile leaf.ext -out leaf.pem`
steps.explain: Root first (self-signed), then the intermediate signed by the root, then the leaf signed by the intermediate. The intermediate's CSR does not depend on the root, so making it earlier is also accepted, and so is verifying before you write the fullchain. The fullchain is leaf first; the root stays out of it.

steps.prompt: Complete the command that signs `leaf.csr` with the intermediate.
code: openssl x509 __1__ -in leaf.csr -CA int.pem __2__ int.key __3__ -days 200 -sha256 __4__ leaf.ext -out leaf.pem
steps.explain: `-req` says the input is a CSR. `-signkey` would self-sign instead of using the CA.
hints: The CA certificate is `-CA`; its private key has a matching flag.

steps.prompt: Which extfile lines belong in `int.ext` (the intermediate) and which in `leaf.ext`?
`openssl verify -CAfile root.pem leaf.pem` prints this. Which flag, with which file, is missing? Type just the flag.
code: error 20 at 0 depth lookup: unable to get local issuer certificate
steps.explain: Error 20 at depth 0: openssl could not find the leaf's issuer. Pass the intermediate with `-untrusted int.pem` ("untrusted" because it is a link to check, not an anchor to trust).

steps.prompt: You put `-addext "subjectAltName=..."` in the CSR, signed it with `openssl x509 -req ... -extfile leaf.ext`, and the certificate has **no SAN**. `leaf.ext` has only basicConstraints, keyUsage and EKU. Why?
options: `x509 -req` does not copy extensions from the CSR; add the SAN to the extfile or use `-copy_extensions copy`
The intermediate's pathlen strips the SAN
steps.explain: A CA decides what goes in the certificate; copying requested extensions blindly would let a requester ask for `CA:TRUE`. .NET's `LoadSigningRequestPem` makes the same choice by default.

steps.title: The same pipeline in .NET
body: | Make a CSR | `openssl req -new -key k -subj ... -out r.csr` | `req.CreateSigningRequestPem()` |
| Read a CSR | `openssl req -in r.csr -noout -text -verify` | `CertificateRequest.LoadSigningRequestPem(pem, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256)` |
| Sign with a CA | `openssl x509 -req -CA ca.pem -CAkey ca.key -extfile x.ext` | add extensions, then `req.Create(ca, notBefore, notAfter, serial)` |
| Verify | `openssl verify -CAfile root.pem -untrusted int.pem leaf.pem` | `X509Chain` with `CustomRootTrust`, root in `CustomTrustStore`, int in `ExtraStore` |
// req.SubjectName and req.PublicKey come from the CSR; extensions do not (by default)

code: var req = new CertificateRequest("CN=shop.example", key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
steps.explain: A CSR's PEM label is `CERTIFICATE REQUEST`. By default the requested SAN is dropped, exactly like `openssl x509 -req` without `-copy_extensions`.

steps.title: Sign a CSR like `openssl x509 -req -extfile`
prompt: Write `X509Certificate2 SignCsr(string csrPem, X509Certificate2 ca, string[] dns)`: the .NET version of signing `leaf.csr` with `leaf.ext`.
- load the CSR with `CertificateRequest.LoadSigningRequestPem(csrPem, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256)` (default options: the CSR's own extensions are ignored)

- add the extfile's extensions: Basic Constraints not a CA (critical), Key Usage `DigitalSignature` (critical), EKU serverAuth `1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1`, a SAN with every name in `dns`, and an AKI from `ca`
- sign with `ca`, valid **2030-01-01 to 2031-01-01 UTC**, serial `new byte[] { 0x42 }`
- return the certificate as `Create` gives it (public only: the private key stays with whoever made the CSR)
The tests make a CA and a CSR, then check the result and validate it for serverAuth.
starter: X509Certificate2 SignCsr(string csrPem, X509Certificate2 ca, string[] dns)
solution: X509Certificate2 SignCsr(string csrPem, X509Certificate2 ca, string[] dns)
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid("1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1") }, false));
hints: `return req.Create(ca, new DateTimeOffset(2030, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero), new DateTimeOffset(2031, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, TimeSpan.Zero), new byte[] { 0x42 });`
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true, nbYear: 2029, naYear: 2040);
var dojoCa = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true, nbYear: 2029, naYear: 2035);
var dojoReq = new CertificateRequest("CN=shop.example", dojoKey, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
Dojo.Eq("subject comes from the CSR", "CN=shop.example", dojoLeaf.Subject);
Dojo.Eq("issuer is the CA", "CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoLeaf.Issuer);

Dojo.Check("not a CA, even though the CSR asked for CA:TRUE", dojoBc != null && !dojoBc.CertificateAuthority, "add X509BasicConstraintsExtension(false, false, 0, true) and load the CSR with default options");
Dojo.Check("validates for serverAuth", dojoChain.Build(dojoLeaf), string.Join(",", dojoChain.ChainStatus.Select(s => s.Status)));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: `openssl verify` in .NET
prompt: Write `bool OpensslVerify(X509Certificate2 caFile, X509Certificate2 untrusted, X509Certificate2 leaf)`, the twin of

Use an `X509Chain` with `CustomRootTrust`, `caFile` as the only trust anchor, `untrusted` in `ExtraStore`, `RevocationMode.NoCheck`, `DisableCertificateDownloads = true`, and `VerificationTime` **2030-06-01 00:00 UTC**. Return whether the chain builds.
starter: bool OpensslVerify(X509Certificate2 caFile, X509Certificate2 untrusted, X509Certificate2 leaf)
solution: bool OpensslVerify(X509Certificate2 caFile, X509Certificate2 untrusted, X509Certificate2 leaf)
template: var dojoRoot = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true, naYear: 2040);
var dojoInt = DojoCert("CN=Dojo Issuing CA", dojoRoot, true);
var dojoLeaf = DojoCert("CN=shop.example", dojoInt, false, "shop.example", nbYear: 2030, naYear: 2031);
var dojoOther = DojoCert("CN=Other Root", null, true);
Dojo.Eq("good chain verifies", true, OpensslVerify(dojoRoot, dojoInt, dojoLeaf));
Dojo.Eq("wrong -CAfile fails", false, OpensslVerify(dojoOther, dojoInt, dojoLeaf));
Dojo.Eq("wrong -untrusted fails (error 20)", false, OpensslVerify(dojoRoot, dojoOther, dojoLeaf));
Dojo.Eq("checks the date (2030-06-01)", false, OpensslVerify(dojoRoot, dojoInt, DojoCert("CN=late.example", dojoInt, false, "late.example", nbYear: 2031, naYear: 2032)));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
